title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI gating and quality regression checks
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: recent incidents and a spike in user-reported regressions called out that per-prompt quality drops are often missed by coarse aggregate evals. This PR adds a per-prompt CI gating step to the eval-harness pipeline so that changes which cause significant regressions on individual prompts fail CI and require explicit review. Summary of changes: - New CI hook (eval-harness/ci/per_prompt_gate.py) that computes per-prompt deltas against baseline metrics and fails when thresholds are exceeded. - GitHub Actions workflow (ci/workflows/eval-harness.yml) extended with a per-prompt gating job that runs lightweight evals and uploads summarized metrics as artifacts. - Unit + integration tests (tests/eval/test_prompt_gating.py) and small synthetic prompt set for determinism. - Docs and runbook (docs/processes/eval-gating.md and eval-harness/README.md) describing thresholds, skip-label semantics, and how to triage failures. - Small refactor in eval-harness/core/metrics.py to export prompt-level metric IDs used by the gate. Checklist: - [x] Add per-prompt gate implementation - [x] Wire into GH Actions and test on staging - [x] Add unit tests and integration smoke tests - [x] Add docs and runbook - [x] Add ability to opt-out via label [ci skip-eval] Behavior: Default gate fails the PR if any prompt shows a relative quality delta worse than 7% AND an absolute regressions count above 3 prompts. Thresholds are configurable via the workflow inputs and Linear feature flags. The gate uploads a JSON summary artifact with per-prompt metrics and a human-friendly HTML report (for on-call troubleshooting). Usage notes: maintainers can force-merge with the "ci:eval-override" label after a documented triage (see docs/processes/eval-gating.md). Related: ENG-8421 (per-prompt alerting epic), ENG-8500 (eval-harness infra improvements), SUP-4321 (customer-reported regression).
